newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX rebounds after three-day fall.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX rebounds after three-day fall.

text.p: Hungarian share prices rebounded from a three-day slump on Wednesday to close a little higher as recent low share prices induced some new purchases, traders said.
The BUX index, which fell 319 points in three days, on Wednesday closed at 5,187.89 points, up 47.63.
"More foreigners were on the buying side than before but at the same time selling orders...remained," said Geza Raner of Bank Austria-GiroCredit.
Both he and another trader said the market's rise today did not necessarily mean a breakthrough.
"Many people think to buy at these prices," one trader said earlier. "But at the same time the selling side was still quite strong."
The Budapest Stock Exchange once again bucked the trend of leading European markets.
"Foreign bourses have lost their direction-setting role (on the Budapest bourse) and this is not necessarily a problem," Raner said.
"But it's clear that Hungarian share prices fall because prices rose too sharply too suddenly in January and in early February...meanwhile there aren't any fresh news on the market," he said.

The BUX index of the Budapest bourse, which rose more than 100 percent in dollar terms in 1996, rose to a life-high of 5,815.38 points on February 5, 1997 from 4,134.31 points at the end of December 1996.

In addition, the next phase of a sell-off in the shares of oil company MOL was keeping many investors on the sidelines, traders said, adding that a substantial change in the market's pattern was unlikely until then.
MOL's price is seen trading rangebound, whereas usually the shares of the largest capitalised issue on the bourse show direction to the rest of the market.
Wednesday's gainers included banks, with Inter-Europa rising 4,350 forints to end at 47,950 and OTP gaining 105 forints to finish at 3,505.
Chemicals also firmed, with Borsodchem advancing 50 forints to 6,150 and TVK gaining 60 to end at 2,160.
MOL shares closed at 3,055 forints, down 10.
